subject: math
intro: Eight multiple-choice questions on describing data distributions by center, spread, and shape, and on identifying clusters, gaps, peaks, and outliers.

items.prompt:
The number of books seven students read over the summer was $3, 4, 5, 5, 5, 6, 7$. What is the median (a typical value, the center) of this data set?
A) $5$
B) $4$
C) $7$
D) $\frac{35}{7}$

steps: The data are already in order: $3, 4, 5, 5, 5, 6, 7$.
With $7$ values, the median is the $4$th value (the middle one), which is $5$.
So a typical value (the center) is $5$ books, choice A.
B) $4$ is just one of the smaller values, not the middle one.
C) $7$ is the maximum, not the center.
D) $\frac{35}{7}=5$ is actually the mean here, which also equals $5$, but it is described as a division and is not the median; the question asks for the median, so A is the best, clearest answer.

items.prompt:
The daily high temperatures for a week were $68, 70, 71, 72, 73, 90, 95$ degrees. What is the range (a measure of spread)?
A) $27$
B) $68$ to $95$
C) $73$
D) $95$

steps: The range is the difference between the largest and smallest values.
Maximum is $95$ and minimum is $68$.
Range $= 95 - 68 = 27$ degrees, choice A.
B) '$68$ to $95$' lists the endpoints instead of computing their difference; the range is a single number.
C) $73$ is just one of the middle values, not a measure of spread.
D) $95$ is only the maximum, not the range.

items.prompt:
On a dot plot of quiz scores, the dots pile up on the right near the high scores and trail off toward the left with a few low scores. What is the shape of this distribution?
A) Skewed left
B) Skewed right
C) Symmetric
D) Uniform

steps: Skew direction is named by the side the tail points toward, not the side where the data pile up.
Here the tail trails off toward the left (the low scores), so the distribution is skewed left, choice A.
B) Skewed right reverses the direction; it would describe a tail pointing toward the high values.
C) Symmetric would require both sides to look about the same, but one side has a long tail.
D) Uniform would mean the dots are spread about evenly, which they are not.

items.prompt:
A dot plot of the number of pets per family shows a tall stack of dots at $0$ and $1$, no dots from $2$ through $8$, and a single dot at $9$. Which description best fits the value at $9$?
A) An outlier, separated from the cluster by a gap
B) The center of the data
C) Part of a symmetric distribution
D) Not unusual, just the largest ordinary value
items.answer: A) An outlier, separated from the cluster by a gap

steps: Most families have $0$ or $1$ pet, forming a tight cluster (peak) on the low end.
There are no values from $2$ to $8$, so a clear gap separates the bulk of the data from the single dot at $9$.
A value that sits far away across a gap from the rest of the data is an outlier, choice A.
B) The center is near $0$ to $1$ where the data pile up, not at $9$.
C) A symmetric distribution would not have one lone point far out on one side.
D) Because a gap clearly separates $9$ from everything else, it is not just an ordinary largest value; it is a genuine outlier.
solution.answer: A) An outlier, separated from the cluster by a gap

items.prompt:
A statistical question produced the data $4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 6, 7, 8$ hours of sleep. What is the mean (the average) of this data set?
A) $\frac{47}{8} = 5.875$
B) $47$
C) $6$
D) $\frac{47}{4} = 11.75$

steps: There are $8$ data points, so divide the sum by $8$: $\frac{47}{8} = 5.875$, choice A.
B) $47$ is the sum before dividing by the number of values, so it is not the mean.
C) $6$ is the median (the middle value), not the mean the question asks for.
D) $\frac{47}{4}$ divides by $4$ instead of by the correct count of $8$ data points.
Skewed right means the data pile up at the low end and a long tail stretches toward the high values.
In $\{1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 9\}$ most values are small ($1, 2, 3$) and a long tail reaches up to $9$, so it is skewed right, choice A.
B) $\{2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4\}$ is roughly symmetric around $3$, with no long tail.
C) $\{5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5\}$ has all equal values, so there is no skew at all.
D) $\{1, 4, 4, 4, 4, 7, 7\}$ is fairly balanced around $4$ and does not have a single long tail on the high side.

items.prompt:
For the data set $\{1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 9\}$, the mean is about $2.7$ and the median is $2$. Because of the value $9$, which measure better represents a typical value, and why?
A) The median $2$, because the outlier $9$ pulls the mean upward away from the cluster of low values
B) The mean $2.7$, because the mean is always the best typical value
C) The mean $2.7$, because it uses every value
D) The range $8$, because it shows the typical value
items.answer: A) The median $2$, because the outlier $9$ pulls the mean upward away from the cluster of low values

steps: Six of the seven values lie between $1$ and $3$; the single value $9$ is a high outlier.
The mean $\approx 2.7$ is pulled upward by the $9$, so it sits above where most of the data actually are.
The median $2$ stays near the cluster of low values, so it better represents a typical value, choice A.
B) The mean is not always best; a strong outlier can drag it away from the bulk of the data.
C) Using every value is exactly why the mean gets distorted here by the outlier $9$.
D) The range $9-1=8$ measures spread, not a typical value (center), so it cannot answer this question.
solution.answer: A) The median $2$, because the outlier $9$ pulls the mean upward away from the cluster of low values

items.prompt:
A dot plot shows students' ages clustered symmetrically around $11$, ranging from $9$ to $13$ with the tallest stack at $11$. Which statement correctly gives the center, spread, and shape together?
A) Center about $11$ years; range $13 - 9 = 4$ years; shape roughly symmetric
B) Center about $4$ years; range $11$ years; shape skewed right
C) Center about $11$ years; range '$9$ to $13$'; shape skewed left
D) Center about $13$ years; range $4$ years; shape uniform
items.answer: A) Center about $11$ years; range $13 - 9 = 4$ years; shape roughly symmetric

steps: Center: the data cluster around $11$ with the tallest stack there, so a typical value is about $11$ years.
Spread: the range is $\max - \min = 13 - 9 = 4$ years.
Shape: the dots are balanced around the peak at $11$, so the distribution is roughly symmetric. All three match choice A.
B) confuses center with spread, reporting the range $4$ as the center and calling it skewed when it is symmetric.
C) lists the range as '$9$ to $13$' (the endpoints) instead of their difference $4$, and a symmetric shape is not skewed left.
D) puts the center at the maximum $13$ instead of $11$, and a single tall peak in the middle is not uniform.
solution.answer: A) Center about $11$ years; range $13 - 9 = 4$ years; shape roughly symmetric
